Natural_Language: This part prescribes procedures for extraordinary contractual actions under Pub. L. 85-804 and implements SAFETY Act liability protections.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_000: Part 50 scope covers extraordinary contractual actions and SAFETY Act
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. Part 50 has two major components: extraordinary contractual actions (Subpart 50.1) and SAFETY Act (Subpart 50.2). Conjunction captures both as required scope.

Natural_Language: This part prescribes procedures and implements statutory and Executive Order requirements for extraordinary emergency authority and indemnification authority for qualified anti-terrorism technology.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_000_a: Part prescribes procedures for extraordinary emergency authority and indemnification for anti-terrorism technology
Validation_Notes: Parent for two subparagraphs. Both prescriptive functions are conjunctive requirements of this part.

Natural_Language: Prescribes procedures and implements statutory and Executive Order requirements for entering into, amending, or modifying contracts in order to facilitate the national defense under the extraordinary emergency authority granted by Public Law 85-804 (50 U.S.C. 1431-1435) and Executive Order 10789, dated November 14, 1958. It does not cover advance payments (see Subpart 32.4).
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_000_a_1_a: Part prescribes procedures for entering into, amending, or modifying contracts to facilitate national defense under Pub. L. 85-804 and E.O. 10789; P_50_000_a_1_b: Part does not cover advance payments
Validation_Notes: Scope statement with explicit exclusion. The advance payments exclusion (negation) is an important scope limiter referencing Subpart 32.4.

Natural_Language: Implements indemnification authority granted by Pub. L. 85-804 and paragraph 1A of E.O. 10789 with respect to any matter that has been, or could be, designated by the Secretary of Homeland Security as a qualified anti-terrorism technology as defined in the SAFETY Act.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_000_a_2: Part implements indemnification authority under Pub. L. 85-804 and E.O. 10789 paragraph 1A for qualified anti-terrorism technology
Validation_Notes: Atomic scope statement. Indemnification authority is specific to matters designated or potentially designated as QATT by Secretary of Homeland Security.

Natural_Language: Implements SAFETY Act liability protections to promote development and use of anti-terrorism technologies.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_000_b: Part implements SAFETY Act liability protections for anti-terrorism technologies
Validation_Notes: Atomic scope statement. Second major component of Part 50.

Natural_Language: Definitions used in this part.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_100: Part 50 definitions
Validation_Notes: Parent for two definitions in Subpart 50.1.

Natural_Language: Approving authority means an agency official or contract adjustment board authorized to approve actions under Pub. L. 85-804 and E.O. 10789.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_100_aa_a: Approving authority is an agency official authorized to approve actions under Pub. L. 85-804 and E.O. 10789; P_50_100_aa_b: Approving authority is a contract adjustment board authorized to approve actions under Pub. L. 85-804 and E.O. 10789
Validation_Notes: Definitional disjunction. Either an agency official or a contract adjustment board qualifies as approving authority.

Natural_Language: Secretarial level means a level at or above the level of a deputy assistant agency head, or a contract adjustment board.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_100_sl_a: Secretarial level is at or above deputy assistant agency head level; P_50_100_sl_b: Secretarial level includes a contract adjustment board
Validation_Notes: Definitional disjunction. Secretarial level can be satisfied by position level or by being a contract adjustment board.

Natural_Language: General provisions for extraordinary contractual actions.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_101: General provisions parent
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition aggregating authority, policy, and records subsections.

Natural_Language: Authority for extraordinary contractual actions.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_101_1: Authority provisions parent
Validation_Notes: Parent for two authority provisions: Presidential empowerment and E.O. delegation.

Natural_Language: Pub. L. 85-804 empowers the President to authorize agencies exercising functions in connection with the national defense to enter into, amend, and modify contracts, without regard to other provisions of law related to making, performing, amending, or modifying contracts, whenever the President considers that such action would facilitate the national defense.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_101_1_a_a: Pub. L. 85-804 empowers President to authorize agencies to enter into, amend, and modify contracts; P_50_101_1_a_b: Authorization is without regard to other provisions of law; P_50_101_1_a_c: President considers action would facilitate national defense
Validation_Notes: Conditional authority. Presidential determination that action facilitates national defense triggers broad authority to override other contracting laws. HIGH-RISK due to Rule 15 and the extraordinary breadth of authority granted.

Natural_Language: E.O. 10789 authorizes the heads of the following agencies to exercise the authority conferred by Pub. L. 85-804 and to delegate it to other officials within the agency: the Government Publishing Office; the Department of Homeland Security; the Tennessee Valley Authority; the National Aeronautics and Space Administration; the General Services Administration; the Defense, Army, Navy, Air Force, Treasury, Interior, Agriculture, Commerce, and Transportation Departments; the Department of Energy for functions transferred to that Department from other authorized agencies; and any other agency that may be authorized by the President.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_101_1_b_a: E.O. 10789 authorizes specified agency heads to exercise Pub. L. 85-804 authority; P_50_101_1_b_b: Authorized agency heads may delegate authority to other officials within the agency
Validation_Notes: Conjunctive delegation. Both the direct exercise authority and the delegation authority are granted simultaneously. List of specific agencies is enumerated in the natural language text.

Natural_Language: Policy for extraordinary contractual actions.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_101_2: Policy provisions parent
Validation_Notes: Parent for two policy provisions.

Natural_Language: Actions authorized under Pub. L. 85-804 shall be accomplished as expeditiously as practicable, consistent with the exercise of sound judgment appropriate to the use of such extraordinary authority.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_101_2_a_a: Actions under Pub. L. 85-804 shall be accomplished as expeditiously as practicable; P_50_101_2_a_b: Actions shall be consistent with exercise of sound judgment appropriate to extraordinary authority
Validation_Notes: Mandatory conjunction. Both expeditiousness and sound judgment are required simultaneously. 'Shall' creates binding obligation.

Natural_Language: Certain kinds of relief previously available only under Pub. L. 85-804 are now available under 41 U.S.C. chapter 71, Contract Disputes. The disputes process in part 33 must be followed before pursuing extraordinary contract relief under this part because the authority under Pub. L. 85-804 may not be relied upon when other adequate legal authority exists. The contracting officer should seek legal advice when unsure as to whether part 33 applies.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_101_2_b_a: Disputes process in part 33 must be followed before pursuing extraordinary relief under this part; P_50_101_2_b_b: Authority under Pub. L. 85-804 may not be relied upon when other adequate legal authority exists; P_50_101_2_b_c: Contracting officer should seek legal advice when unsure whether part 33 applies
Validation_Notes: Conditional with advisory. When adequate legal authority exists (antecedent), Part 33 disputes process is mandatory (consequent). The advisory 'should' for legal advice is conjunctive but non-binding. HIGH-RISK due to Rule 15 and the precedence requirement.

Natural_Language: Agencies must maintain complete records of all actions taken under this Subpart 50.1. For each request for relief processed, these records must include, at a minimum, the contractor's request, all relevant memorandums, the Memorandum of Decision, and a copy of the contractual document implementing an approved request.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_101_3: Agencies must maintain complete records of all actions under Subpart 50.1
Validation_Notes: Parent mandatory conjunction. 'Must' creates binding obligation. All four record elements required at minimum.

Natural_Language: The contractor's request.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_101_3_a: Records must include the contractor's request
Validation_Notes: Atomic mandatory record element.

Natural_Language: All relevant memorandums, correspondence, affidavits, and other pertinent documents.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_101_3_b: Records must include all relevant memorandums, correspondence, affidavits, and other pertinent documents
Validation_Notes: Atomic mandatory record element. Broad scope captures all relevant documentation.

Natural_Language: The Memorandum of Decision (see 50.103-6 and 50.104-2).
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_101_3_c: Records must include the Memorandum of Decision
Validation_Notes: Atomic mandatory record element with cross-references to 50.103-6 and 50.104-2.

Natural_Language: A copy of the contractual document implementing an approved request.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_101_3_d: Records must include copy of contractual document implementing approved request
Validation_Notes: Atomic mandatory record element.

Natural_Language: Delegation of and limitations on exercise of authority under Pub. L. 85-804 and E.O. 10789.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_102: Delegation and limitations parent
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating delegation, boards, and limitations subsections.

Natural_Language: An agency head may delegate in writing authority under Pub. L. 85-804 and E.O. 10789, subject to limitations.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_102_1: Agency head delegation authority parent
Validation_Notes: Parent for four delegation limitations. Permissive 'may' for delegation itself, but limitations are mandatory.

Natural_Language: Authority delegated must be to a level high enough to ensure uniformity of action.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_102_1_a: Delegated authority must be to level ensuring uniformity of action
Validation_Notes: Mandatory atomic requirement. 'Must' creates binding obligation on delegation level.

Natural_Language: Authority to approve requests to obligate the Government in excess of $90,000 may not be delegated below the secretarial level.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_102_1_b_a: Request obligates Government in excess of $90,000; P_50_102_1_b_b: Authority is delegated below secretarial level
Validation_Notes: Conditional prohibition. When obligation exceeds $90K threshold, delegation below secretarial level is prohibited. HIGH-RISK due to Rule 15.

Natural_Language: Regardless of dollar amount, authority to approve any amendment without consideration that increases the contract price or unit price may not be delegated below the secretarial level, except in extraordinary cases or classes of cases when the agency head finds that special circumstances clearly justify such delegation.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_102_1_c_a: Amendment without consideration increases contract price or unit price; P_50_102_1_c_b: Authority delegated below secretarial level; P_50_102_1_c_c: Agency head finds special circumstances clearly justify delegation
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Conditional prohibition with exception. Default prohibition on delegation below secretarial level for price-increasing amendments without consideration. Exception requires agency head finding of special circumstances. Complex nested logic with HIGH-RISK transformation.

Natural_Language: Regardless of dollar amount, authority to indemnify against unusually hazardous or nuclear risks, including extension of such indemnification to subcontracts, must be exercised only by the Secretary or Administrator of the agency concerned, the Public Printer, or the Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Tennessee Valley Authority (see 50.104-3).
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_102_1_d_a: Authority involves indemnification against unusually hazardous or nuclear risks; P_50_102_1_d_b: Authority is exercised by Secretary/Administrator, Public Printer, or TVA Chairman
Validation_Notes: Conditional restriction on who may exercise indemnification authority. Non-delegable. 'Must be exercised only by' is an exclusive mandate. HIGH-RISK due to Rule 15.

Natural_Language: An agency head may establish a contract adjustment board with authority to approve, authorize, and direct appropriate action under this Subpart 50.1 and to make all appropriate determinations and findings. The decisions of the board must not be subject to appeal; however, the board may reconsider and modify, correct, or reverse its previous decisions. The board must determine its own procedures and have authority to take all action necessary or appropriate to conduct its functions.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_102_2_a: Agency head may establish contract adjustment board; P_50_102_2_b: Board has authority to approve, authorize, and direct action under Subpart 50.1; P_50_102_2_c: Board decisions not subject to appeal; P_50_102_2_d: Board may reconsider and modify its decisions; P_50_102_2_e: Board determines its own procedures
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Mixed permissive and mandatory. Establishment is discretionary (tautology). If established, board authorities and non-appealability are mandatory. Board reconsideration is discretionary. Complex structure with multiple modal verbs.

Natural_Language: Limitations on exercise of authority under Pub. L. 85-804.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_102_3: Limitations parent
Validation_Notes: Parent for five limitation categories. All limitations apply simultaneously.

Natural_Language: Pub. L. 85-804 is not authority for the prohibited actions listed in (a)(1) through (a)(4).
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_102_3_a: Pub. L. 85-804 prohibitions parent
Validation_Notes: Parent for four absolute prohibitions. All apply simultaneously as scope limitations.

Natural_Language: Using a cost-plus-a-percentage-of-cost system of contracting.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_102_3_a_1: Pub. L. 85-804 is not authority for cost-plus-percentage-of-cost contracting
Validation_Notes: Absolute prohibition. Negation of this contracting method under Pub. L. 85-804 authority.

Natural_Language: Making any contract that violates existing law limiting profit or fees.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_102_3_a_2: Pub. L. 85-804 is not authority for contracts violating profit/fee limits
Validation_Notes: Absolute prohibition. Cannot use extraordinary authority to override profit/fee limitations.

Natural_Language: Providing for other than full and open competition for award of contracts for supplies or services.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_102_3_a_3: Pub. L. 85-804 is not authority for other than full and open competition
Validation_Notes: Absolute prohibition. Cannot circumvent competition requirements.

Natural_Language: Waiving any bid bond, payment bond, performance bond, or other bond required by law.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_102_3_a_4: Pub. L. 85-804 is not authority for waiving required bonds
Validation_Notes: Absolute prohibition. Bond requirements are inviolable even under extraordinary authority.

Natural_Language: No contract, amendment, or modification shall be made under Pub. L. 85-804's authority unless conditions in (b)(1) through (b)(4) are met.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_102_3_b: Preconditions for any action under Pub. L. 85-804 parent
Validation_Notes: Parent for mandatory preconditions. All four must be satisfied for any action under this authority.

Natural_Language: Unless the approving authority finds that the action will facilitate the national defense.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_102_3_b_1_a: Approving authority finds action will facilitate national defense; P_50_102_3_b_1_b: Contract/amendment/modification is made under Pub. L. 85-804
Validation_Notes: Necessary condition expressed as 'unless'. Without the national defense finding, no action permitted. Equivalent to: action permitted only if finding made. HIGH-RISK due to Rule 15.

Natural_Language: Unless other legal authority within the agency concerned is deemed to be lacking or inadequate.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_102_3_b_2_a: Other legal authority within agency is lacking or inadequate; P_50_102_3_b_2_b: Action under Pub. L. 85-804 is permitted
Validation_Notes: Necessary condition. Extraordinary authority is a last resort; other legal authority must be absent or inadequate. HIGH-RISK due to Rule 15.

Natural_Language: Except within the limits of the amounts appropriated and the statutory contract authorization (however, indemnification agreements authorized by an agency head (50.104-3) are not limited to amounts appropriated or to contract authorization).
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_102_3_b_3_a: Action must be within limits of amounts appropriated and statutory contract authorization; P_50_102_3_b_3_b: Indemnification agreements under 50.104-3 are exempt from appropriation and authorization limits
Validation_Notes: General fiscal limitation with explicit carve-out for indemnification agreements. The exception for 50.104-3 indemnification is significant and must be noted.

Natural_Language: That will obligate the Government for any amount over $150 million unless the Senate and House Committees on Armed Services are notified in writing of the proposed obligation and 60 days of continuous session of Congress have passed since the transmittal of such notification. However, this paragraph (b)(4) does not apply to indemnification agreements authorized under 50.104-3.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_102_3_b_4_a: Obligation exceeds $150 million; P_50_102_3_b_4_b: Senate and House Armed Services Committees notified in writing; P_50_102_3_b_4_c: 60 days of continuous Congressional session have passed since notification; P_50_102_3_b_4_d: Action is indemnification agreement under 50.104-3
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Complex conditional with exception. Obligations over $150M trigger Congressional notification and waiting period requirements, but indemnification agreements are exempt. HIGH-RISK due to Rule 15 and fiscal significance.

Natural_Language: No contract shall be amended or modified unless the contractor submits a request before all obligations (including final payment) under the contract have been discharged. No amendment or modification shall increase the contract price to an amount higher than the lowest rejected bid of any responsible bidder, if the contract was negotiated under 14.404-1(f).
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_102_3_c_a: Contractor submits request before all obligations discharged; P_50_102_3_c_b: Contract is amended or modified; P_50_102_3_c_c: Contract was negotiated under 14.404-1(f); P_50_102_3_c_d: Amendment increases price above lowest rejected bid of responsible bidder
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Two independent restrictions in conjunction. First: timing restriction on requests (must be before obligations discharged). Second: conditional price ceiling for contracts negotiated under 14.404-1(f). HIGH-RISK due to dual Rule 15 applications.

Natural_Language: No informal commitment will be formalized unless conditions in (d)(1) and (d)(2) are met.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_102_3_d: Informal commitment formalization preconditions parent
Validation_Notes: Parent for two mandatory preconditions for formalizing informal commitments. Both must be satisfied.

Natural_Language: The contractor submits a written request for payment within 6 months after furnishing, or arranging to furnish, supplies or services in reliance upon the commitment.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_102_3_d_1: Contractor submits written payment request within 6 months after furnishing supplies/services
Validation_Notes: Atomic mandatory timing requirement. Six-month window is a hard deadline.

Natural_Language: The approving authority finds that, at the time the commitment was made, it was impracticable to use normal contracting procedures.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_102_3_d_2: Approving authority finds it was impracticable to use normal contracting procedures at time of commitment
Validation_Notes: Atomic mandatory finding. Impracticability determination must be retrospective to time commitment was made.

Natural_Language: No executive department or agency will exercise the indemnification authority granted under paragraph 1A of E.O. 10789 with respect to any supply or service that has been, or could be, designated by the Secretary of Homeland Security as a qualified anti-terrorism technology unless conditions in (e)(1) or (e)(2) are met.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_102_3_e: QATT indemnification restriction parent
Validation_Notes: Parent for two alternative exception paths. Disjunction because DoD and non-DoD agencies have different approval pathways.

Natural_Language: For the Department of Defense, the Secretary of Defense has determined that the exercise of authority under E.O. 10789 is necessary for the timely and effective conduct of the United States military or intelligence activities, after consideration of the authority provided under the SAFETY Act.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_102_3_e_1_a: Department is DoD; P_50_102_3_e_1_b: Secretary of Defense determines exercise necessary for military/intelligence activities; P_50_102_3_e_1_c: SAFETY Act authority has been considered
Validation_Notes: DoD-specific exception path. Secretary of Defense must make necessity determination AND consider SAFETY Act alternatives. HIGH-RISK due to Rule 15.

Natural_Language: For other departments and agencies that have authority under E.O. 10789: the Secretary of Homeland Security has advised whether the use of the authority under the SAFETY Act would be appropriate, and the Director of the Office of Management and Budget has approved the exercise of authority under the Executive order.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_102_3_e_2_a: Department/agency is not DoD and has E.O. 10789 authority; P_50_102_3_e_2_b: Secretary of Homeland Security has advised on SAFETY Act appropriateness; P_50_102_3_e_2_c: OMB Director has approved exercise of authority
Validation_Notes: Non-DoD exception path. Requires both DHS advice and OMB approval. Two-agency concurrence requirement. HIGH-RISK due to Rule 15.

Natural_Language: This section prescribes standards and procedures for processing contractors' requests for contract adjustment under Pub. L. 85-804 and E.O. 10789.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_103: Contract adjustments parent
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating all contract adjustment subsections 50.103-1 through 50.103-7.

Natural_Language: The fact that losses occur under a contract is not sufficient basis for exercising the authority conferred by Pub. L. 85-804. Whether appropriate action will facilitate the national defense is a judgment to be made on the basis of all of the facts of the case. Although it is impossible to predict or enumerate all the types of cases in which action may be appropriate, examples are included in 50.103-2. Even if all of the factors in any of the examples are present, other considerations may warrant denying a contractor's request for contract adjustment.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_103_1_a: Contract losses alone are not sufficient basis for Pub. L. 85-804 authority; P_50_103_1_b: National defense facilitation is determined based on all facts of the case; P_50_103_1_c: Presence of example factors does not guarantee adjustment approval
Validation_Notes: Policy statement establishing that losses are insufficient (negation), judgment is holistic, and examples are not dispositive. Conjunction of three independent policy principles.

Natural_Language: Types of contract adjustment available under Pub. L. 85-804.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_103_2: Types of contract adjustment parent
Validation_Notes: Parent for three types: amendments without consideration, correcting mistakes, and formalizing informal commitments.

Natural_Language: Amendments without consideration.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_103_2_a: Amendments without consideration parent
Validation_Notes: Parent for two amendment-without-consideration scenarios.

Natural_Language: When an actual or threatened loss under a defense contract, however caused, will impair the productive ability of a contractor whose continued performance on any defense contract or whose continued operation as a source of supply is found to be essential to the national defense, the contract may be amended without consideration, but only to the extent necessary to avoid such impairment to the contractor's productive ability.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_103_2_a_1_a: Actual or threatened loss will impair contractor's productive ability; P_50_103_2_a_1_b: Contractor's continued performance/operation is essential to national defense; P_50_103_2_a_1_c: Contract is amended without consideration; P_50_103_2_a_1_d: Amendment is only to extent necessary to avoid impairment
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Permissive authority with constraint. 'May' creates discretion (tautology) but the 'only to extent necessary' qualifier limits scope. Both impairment and essentiality must be present. HIGH-RISK due to Rule 15.

Natural_Language: When a contractor suffers a loss (not merely a decrease in anticipated profits) under a defense contract because of Government action, the character of the action will generally determine whether any adjustment in the contract will be made, and its extent. When the Government directs its action primarily at the contractor and acts in its capacity as the other contracting party, the contract may be adjusted in the interest of fairness.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_103_2_a_2_a: Contractor suffers actual loss due to Government action; P_50_103_2_a_2_b: Government action directed primarily at contractor in contracting party capacity; P_50_103_2_a_2_c: Contract is adjusted in interest of fairness
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Permissive authority. 'May be adjusted' creates discretion. Requires actual loss (not just decreased profits) from Government action directed at contractor. Fairness standard is subjective. HIGH-RISK due to Rule 15.

Natural_Language: Correcting mistakes. A contract may be amended or modified to correct or mitigate the effect of a mistake.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_103_2_b: Correcting mistakes parent
Validation_Notes: Parent for mistake correction examples and policy.

Natural_Language: A contract may be amended or modified to correct or mitigate the effect of a mistake. Examples: (i) failure to express agreement clearly in writing, (ii) contractor mistake obvious to contracting officer, (iii) mutual mistake as to material fact.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_103_2_b_1_a: Contract is amended to correct/mitigate mistake; P_50_103_2_b_1_b: Mistake is failure to express agreement clearly; P_50_103_2_b_1_c: Mistake is obvious contractor error apparent to CO; P_50_103_2_b_1_d: Mistake is mutual mistake as to material fact
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Disjunction (Disj): Rule 8; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Permissive authority with illustrative examples. Any qualifying mistake type may trigger discretionary amendment. Examples are non-exhaustive. HIGH-RISK due to Rule 15.

Natural_Language: Amending contracts to correct mistakes with the least possible delay normally will facilitate the national defense by expediting the contracting program and assuring contractors that mistakes will be corrected expeditiously and fairly.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_103_2_b_2: Correcting mistakes with least delay normally facilitates national defense
Validation_Notes: Policy statement. 'Normally will facilitate' is advisory/declarative, not a mandatory requirement. Provides policy rationale for expeditious correction.

Natural_Language: Under certain circumstances, informal commitments may be formalized to permit payment to persons who have taken action without a formal contract. An example is when a person, responding to an agency official's written or oral instructions and relying in good faith upon the official's apparent authority, has furnished or arranged to furnish supplies or services without formal contractual coverage.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_103_2_c_a: Person responded to agency official's instructions in good faith; P_50_103_2_c_b: Person relied on official's apparent authority; P_50_103_2_c_c: Person furnished supplies/services without formal contract; P_50_103_2_c_d: Informal commitment is formalized to permit payment
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Permissive authority. 'May be formalized' creates discretion. Three conditions (good faith response, reliance on apparent authority, performance without contract) trigger eligibility but not entitlement. HIGH-RISK due to Rule 15.

Natural_Language: Contractor requests for contract adjustment.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_103_3: Contractor requests parent
Validation_Notes: Parent for request requirements and certification.

Natural_Language: Contractors must submit two copies of requests for contract adjustments to the contracting officer or an authorized representative. The request must state the items listed in (a)(1) through (a)(4).
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_103_3_a_a: Contractor submits two copies to CO or authorized representative; P_50_103_3_a: Request requirements parent
Validation_Notes: Parent for mandatory request content. Must makes all elements binding. Two copies required.

Natural_Language: The precise adjustment requested.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_103_3_a_1: Request must state the precise adjustment requested
Validation_Notes: Atomic mandatory request element.

Natural_Language: The essential facts, summarized chronologically in narrative form.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_103_3_a_2: Request must state essential facts in chronological narrative
Validation_Notes: Atomic mandatory request element. Specifies both content and format.

Natural_Language: The contractor's conclusions based on these facts, showing, in terms of the considerations set forth in 50.103-1 and 50.103-2, when the contractor considers itself entitled to the adjustment.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_103_3_a_3: Request must state contractor conclusions per 50.103-1 and 50.103-2
Validation_Notes: Atomic mandatory request element with cross-references to 50.103-1 and 50.103-2.

Natural_Language: Whether or not: (i) all obligations discharged; (ii) final payment made; (iii) proceeds subject to assignment; and (iv) contractor has sought similar adjustment from GAO or other Government entity.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_103_3_a_4_a: Status of obligation discharge; P_50_103_3_a_4_b: Status of final payment; P_50_103_3_a_4_c: Assignment/transfer of proceeds; P_50_103_3_a_4_d: Prior/anticipated similar claims
Validation_Notes: Mandatory disclosure of four status items. All four must be addressed.

Natural_Language: A contractor seeking a contract adjustment that exceeds the simplified acquisition threshold shall, at the time the request is submitted, submit a certification by a person authorized to certify the request on behalf of the contractor that (1) the request is made in good faith and (2) the supporting data are accurate and complete to the best of that person's knowledge and belief.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_103_3_b_a: Adjustment exceeds simplified acquisition threshold; P_50_103_3_b_b: Certification submitted at time of request; P_50_103_3_b_c: Request is made in good faith; P_50_103_3_b_d: Supporting data are accurate and complete
Validation_Notes: Conditional mandatory certification. Exceeding SAT threshold triggers certification requirement. Shall makes it binding. Certification must be by authorized person. HIGH-RISK due to Rule 15.

Natural_Language: Facts and evidence requirements for contract adjustment requests.
Atomic_Propositions: P_50_103_4: Facts and evidence parent
Validation_Notes: Parent for five categories of facts/evidence requirements corresponding to different request types.

Natural_Language: General.
